headline: A strong Thanksgiving storm is still on track to bring 1–2 inches of rain (locally up to 3) and damaging east wind gusts around 60 mph to New York City and Long Island Thursday afternoon and evening, with widespread coastal flooding Thursday into Friday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Tuesday stays dry as high pressure builds in. North-northwest winds stay gusty this afternoon, gusting around 25–35 mph with isolated gusts near 40 mph, until roughly 3–5 PM, then winds ease to light overnight with dry weather continuing.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Wednesday stays dry, with winds turning northeast at about 10–15 mph. On Thanksgiving (Thursday) rain spreads in from the south through the morning and turns moderate to heavy in the afternoon and evening, totaling 1–2 inches with local amounts near 3 inches; an isolated thunderstorm is possible, and ponding on roads plus widespread minor flooding of poor-drainage areas is expected, though the storm's fairly quick northward movement should limit the overall flood threat. A High Wind Watch remains in effect from Thursday morning through late Thursday night for New York City, Long Island and parts of northeast New Jersey (Hudson and eastern Essex and Union counties), where east winds could gust to 60 mph, or up to 70 mph on Long Island if the stronger computer-model scenario pans out; a new Wind Advisory covers most of the rest of the area (nearby suburbs in New York, New Jersey and Connecticut) from 10 AM Thursday to 5 AM Friday. The worst weather could fall anywhere from about 10 AM Thursday through the overnight, but a surge of dry air from the south should cut off the heavy rain and strongest winds Thursday evening, leaving perhaps light rain or drizzle under low clouds; on Friday, cold air high overhead could spark a few showers (maybe a wet snowflake on the highest hills), with west winds gusting about 30–40 mph.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday stays breezy with west winds gusting roughly 25–35 mph and some low clouds possible. Sunday looks calmer and clearer, with light southwest winds; the discussion says little else about the weekend.

coast: A Coastal Flood Watch is being issued for the entire coastline except southeast Connecticut, and a Coastal Flood Advisory for southeast Connecticut, from Thanksgiving through Friday's daytime high tide. Tides are already running high after Tuesday's full moon, with many spots less than a foot from minor flood levels, so localized minor flooding is possible at Wednesday morning's high tide; widespread minor to moderate flooding is expected with the Thursday and Friday high tides, and the most vulnerable spots on the south shore back bays and western Great South Bay could reach major flood levels, depending on how long onshore east-northeast winds last before turning south-southwest. Beach flooding, erosion and overwash (waves washing over dunes) are expected, with overwash looking isolated for now. For boaters, a Small Craft Advisory continues on parts of the ocean until 6 AM Wednesday with seas around 5 feet, and seas build again Wednesday; a Storm Watch covers all waters Thursday for gusts of 58 mph or more, with seas around 20 feet on the ocean and waves near 10 feet on Long Island Sound in the late afternoon and evening. A southwest gale is possible Friday, especially on eastern waters, easing to small-craft conditions Saturday and possibly below that Sunday.
watch_for: Damaging east wind gusts around 60 mph (possibly 70 mph on Long Island) Thursday afternoon and evening; the High Wind Watch could be upgraded.
Minor to moderate, locally major, coastal flooding at the Thursday and Friday high tides, especially on the south shore back bays.
Exact timing of the storm's peak on Thursday, which forecasters are still refining.
confidence: Forecasters are confident the storm arrives Thanksgiving with heavy rain and strong winds, but less sure about the exact timing and how strong the peak gusts get; quieter weather is expected Wednesday and again by Sunday.
